sentence_stem: Had the editor read the manuscript more carefully,
correct_completion: she would have spotted the inconsistencies in the plot.
full_sentence: Had the editor read the manuscript more carefully, she would have spotted the inconsistencies in the plot.
acceptable_variants: she would have caught the plot holes.
she would have noticed the inconsistencies.

options.text: she spots the inconsistencies in the plot.
options.why_wrong: The present simple does not match the unreal past set by 'Had the editor read'; the main clause needs a conditional perfect.

options.text: she would spot the inconsistencies in the plot.
options.why_wrong: 'would spot' is a conditional but not a perfect form, so it cannot refer back to the unrealized past of the condition.

options.text: she would have spotted the inconsistencies in the plot.
she has been spotting the inconsistencies in the plot.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect continuous describes ongoing action and does not complete an inverted third conditional.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: The inverted third conditional replaces 'If she had read' with 'Had' at the start, so the main clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle. Spanish speakers often drop the perfect auxiliary in this structure, so the main clause must keep both 'have' and the participle.
translation: Si la editora hubiera leído el manuscrito con más atención, habría detectado las incoherencias de la trama.
